questions.text: Economics is primarily concerned with the study of how
options: scarce resources are allocated among competing wants
questions.explanation: Economics studies how people make choices about scarce resources that have alternative uses to satisfy unlimited wants.

questions.text: The opportunity cost of a choice is the
options: total cost of producing the choice
value of the next best alternative forgone
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative sacrificed when a choice is made.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a factor of production
questions.explanation: The four traditional factors of production are land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship. Money facilitates production but is not itself a factor of production.

questions.text: The reward for entrepreneurship is
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs receive profit for organizing production and bearing business risks.

questions.text: A point inside a production possibility curve indicates
questions.explanation: A point inside the PPC means some resources are underutilized, so production is inefficient.

questions.text: If the price of a commodity rises and its quantity demanded falls, this illustrates the
questions.explanation: The law of demand states that, other things being equal, price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions.

questions.text: Which of the following would cause a rightward shift in the demand curve for a normal good
options: Increase in the price of the good
questions.explanation: Demand for a normal good generally increases when consumers' income increases.

questions.text: A movement along a demand curve is caused by a change in
questions.explanation: A change in the commodity's own price causes movement along the demand curve. Other factors shift the curve.

questions.text: When the percentage change in quantity demanded is greater than the percentage change in price, demand is
questions.explanation: Demand is elastic when elasticity is greater than 1, meaning quantity demanded responds proportionately more than price.

questions.text: Which of the following commodities is most likely to have perfectly inelastic demand
questions.explanation: Essential life-saving medicine may be demanded regardless of changes in price, making its demand relatively very inelastic.

questions.text: An increase in the price of a substitute for commodity X will normally
questions.explanation: If the substitute becomes more expensive, consumers tend to switch to commodity X, increasing its demand.

questions.text: Which of the following is likely to increase the supply of a commodity
questions.explanation: Improved technology can reduce production costs and increase productivity, encouraging producers to supply more.

questions.text: Market equilibrium occurs when
questions.explanation: Equilibrium is achieved where the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied.

questions.text: If the government fixes the price of a commodity below its equilibrium price, the likely result is
questions.explanation: A price ceiling below equilibrium encourages demand but discourages supply, resulting in a shortage.

questions.text: A major characteristic of perfect competition is
questions.explanation: Perfect competition is characterized by many buyers and sellers, homogeneous products and relatively free entry and exit.

questions.text: A market structure in which there is only one seller of a commodity is called
questions.explanation: A monopoly exists when a single firm dominates the supply of a commodity or service with no close substitute.

questions.text: One major feature of oligopoly is
questions.explanation: In an oligopoly, there are few dominant firms, so each firm's decisions can significantly affect its competitors.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a fixed cost
questions.explanation: A fixed cost does not change directly with the level of output in the short run. Rent is a common example.

questions.text: Average cost is calculated as
questions.explanation: Average cost = Total Cost ÷ Quantity of Output.

questions.text: The law of diminishing returns applies when
options: one variable factor is increased while other factors remain fixed
questions.explanation: The law states that adding more units of a variable factor to fixed factors eventually causes the marginal product to fall.

questions.text: National income refers to the
options: total money supply in a country
total income earned by the factors of production in a country
questions.explanation: National income measures the income earned by the factors of production from economic activity during a given period.

questions.text: Gross Domestic Product measures the value of
options: all goods produced by citizens anywhere in the world
final goods and services produced within a country's borders
only agricultural goods produced in a country
questions.explanation: GDP measures the market value of final goods and services produced within a country's geographical boundaries during a period.

questions.text: Which of the following is a problem associated with measuring national income in developing countries
questions.explanation: Subsistence production may not involve monetary transactions, making it difficult to accurately measure its value.

questions.text: Inflation is best described as a
options: continuous fall in the general price level
sustained rise in the general price level
rise in the price of one commodity
questions.explanation: Inflation is a persistent increase in the general price level, reducing the purchasing power of money.

questions.text: Demand-pull inflation occurs when
questions.explanation: Demand-pull inflation occurs when aggregate demand grows faster than the economy's ability to produce goods and services.

questions.text: Which of the following is a function of money
questions.explanation: Money serves as a medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value and standard of deferred payment.

questions.text: The most important characteristic of money is its
questions.explanation: For money to function effectively, people must generally accept it as a means of payment.

questions.text: Commercial banks create credit mainly through
questions.explanation: Commercial banks create credit by accepting deposits and using part of them to provide loans and advances.

questions.text: The central bank can control the money supply by
questions.explanation: Changing the cash/reserve requirement affects how much commercial banks can lend and therefore influences the money supply.

questions.text: Which of the following is a direct instrument of monetary policy
questions.explanation: Open market operations involve the central bank buying or selling securities to influence money supply and liquidity.

questions.text: Fiscal policy involves the use of
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy is the government's use of taxation, expenditure and borrowing to influence economic activity.

questions.text: A government budget is said to be in deficit when
questions.explanation: A budget deficit occurs when government expenditure is greater than its revenue during a given period.

questions.text: Which of the following is a direct tax
questions.explanation: A direct tax is imposed directly on the income or wealth of individuals or organizations. Personal income tax is an example.

questions.text: The main purpose of taxation is to
questions.explanation: Government uses taxation primarily to raise revenue, although taxes can also redistribute income and influence economic behaviour.

questions.text: A progressive tax is one in which
options: the tax rate decreases as income increases
the tax rate increases as income increases
questions.explanation: Under a progressive tax system, people with higher incomes pay a higher proportion of their income in tax.

questions.text: International trade occurs mainly because countries
options: differ in resource endowments and production capabilities
questions.explanation: Differences in resources, technology and production costs encourage countries to specialize and trade.

questions.text: The principle of comparative advantage suggests that a country should specialize in producing goods for which it has
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage is based on producing goods at a lower opportunity cost relative to another country.

questions.text: A country has a favourable balance of trade when
questions.explanation: A favourable balance of trade, or trade surplus, occurs when the value of visible exports exceeds visible imports.

questions.text: Which of the following is an invisible item in international trade
questions.explanation: Invisible trade involves services, such as insurance, banking, tourism and transportation.

questions.text: A tariff is a
questions.explanation: A tariff is a tax imposed on imported goods, often used to protect domestic producers or raise government revenue.

questions.text: Balance of payments records
options: all economic transactions between a country and the rest of the world
questions.explanation: The balance of payments records a country's economic transactions with other countries over a specified period.

questions.text: Economic development differs from economic growth because development involves
options: only an increase in money supply
improvements in the quality of life and structural changes
questions.explanation: Economic growth mainly concerns an increase in output, while development includes improvements in living standards, institutions and economic structure.

questions.text: Which of the following is an indicator of economic development
questions.explanation: Indicators such as infant mortality, life expectancy, literacy and per-capita income help measure development.

questions.text: Population census is important to economic planning because it provides information about
options: the size and structure of the population
questions.explanation: Census information helps governments plan for schools, healthcare, housing, employment and other public services.

questions.text: An increase in population can be beneficial to an economy if it results in
options: an increase in the productive labour force
questions.explanation: A growing population can increase the labour force and productive capacity, provided there are adequate jobs and resources.

questions.text: One major reason for the establishment of public corporations is to
options: provide essential services to the public
questions.explanation: Public corporations are often established to provide essential services such as electricity, water or transportation.

questions.text: Privatization involves the
options: transfer of government-owned enterprises to private ownership
transfer of private firms to government
questions.explanation: Privatization involves transferring ownership or control of a state-owned enterprise to private individuals or organizations.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major source of agricultural problems in Nigeria
questions.explanation: Farmers often face difficulties obtaining affordable credit, which limits their ability to purchase inputs and improve production.

questions.text: The main aim of a cooperative society is to
options: promote the economic interests of its members
questions.explanation: Cooperative societies are formed by people who voluntarily work together to promote their common economic interests.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to encourage industrialization in a developing country
options: Availability of skilled labour and capital
questions.explanation: Skilled labour and adequate capital improve productivity and provide the resources needed for industrial development.

questions.text: A student has ₦10,000 and can either purchase a textbook for ₦10,000 or use the money to register for a computer course. If the student chooses the textbook, the opportunity cost of the decision is
options: the knowledge gained from reading the textbook
the computer course that the student could no longer register for
the difference between the cost of the textbook and the course
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the next best alternative forgone. Here, it is the computer course sacrificed.

questions.text: The production possibility frontier of an economy is bowed outward from the origin. This shape is primarily explained by the fact that
options: resources are perfectly mobile between all uses
opportunity cost increases as production of one commodity expands
production always increases at a constant rate
questions.explanation: A bowed-out PPC reflects increasing opportunity cost, because resources are not equally efficient in producing different goods.

questions.text: A consumer's income rises from ₦80,000 to ₦100,000 per month, while the quantity of rice demanded falls from 20kg to 16kg. Based on this information, rice is most likely
questions.explanation: Demand for an inferior good falls when income rises, as consumers substitute better alternatives.

questions.text: The price of a commodity increases from ₦200 to ₦250, causing quantity demanded to fall from 1,000 units to 800 units. Using the percentage method based on the original values, the price elasticity of demand is
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity = 200/1,000 × 100 = 20%. Percentage change in price = 50/200 × 100 = 25%. PED = 20/25 = 0.8.

questions.text: If the demand for a commodity is price inelastic, an increase in its price will most likely result in
questions.explanation: With inelastic demand, the percentage fall in quantity demanded is smaller than the percentage increase in price, so total revenue increases.

questions.text: A farmer produces 10 bags of maize with 5 workers. When the sixth worker is employed, total output rises to 13 bags. The marginal product of the sixth worker is
questions.explanation: Marginal product = Change in total product ÷ Change in labour. Therefore, 13 − 10 = 3 bags.

questions.text: A firm has total fixed cost of ₦20,000 and total variable cost of ₦60,000 when it produces 400 units. Its average total cost is
A producer continues to employ additional units of labour because the marginal revenue product of labour is greater than its wage rate. This implies that the producer is attempting to
questions.explanation: A profit-maximizing firm will employ labour as long as the marginal revenue product exceeds the wage cost.

questions.text: Which of the following situations best illustrates economies of scale
options: A firm's average cost rises as output increases
A firm's average cost falls as output increases
A firm's total cost remains unchanged as output increases
A firm's marginal cost becomes permanently zero
questions.explanation: Economies of scale occur when increasing the scale of production causes long-run average cost to fall.

questions.text: A monopolist is able to maintain a high price partly because
options: entry into the industry is restricted
questions.explanation: Barriers to entry protect a monopolist from new competitors and strengthen its market power.

questions.text: If the government grants a subsidy to producers of a commodity, the immediate effect is likely to be
questions.explanation: A subsidy reduces producers' effective cost, encouraging them to increase supply.

questions.text: A government fixes the maximum price of bread below its equilibrium price. Which combination is most likely to result
questions.explanation: A price ceiling below equilibrium makes bread cheaper, increasing quantity demanded while reducing quantity supplied, creating excess demand or shortage.

questions.text: If the cross elasticity of demand between goods X and Y is positive, the goods are most likely
questions.explanation: A positive cross elasticity means an increase in the price of one good causes demand for the other to rise, indicating substitutability.

questions.text: A government decides to impose a tax on cigarettes mainly to
options: eliminate the need for government expenditure
questions.explanation: Taxes on harmful goods can serve both revenue-generating and corrective purposes by discouraging consumption.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains why the demand for salt is relatively price inelastic
options: Salt takes up a large proportion of household income
Salt is a necessity and constitutes a small proportion of income
Salt is mainly consumed by high-income earners
questions.explanation: Necessities with few substitutes and a small expenditure share tend to have relatively inelastic demand.

questions.text: If a country's real GDP rises from ₦50 trillion to ₦55 trillion while its population remains unchanged, the most direct conclusion is that
options: real output per person has increased
the price level must have fallen
questions.explanation: With population unchanged, an increase in real GDP means real output per person has increased.

questions.text: Which of the following would make GDP a poor measure of the welfare of citizens
options: GDP ignores income distribution and non-market activities
questions.explanation: GDP measures production but does not fully reveal income distribution, environmental quality, leisure or unpaid household work.

questions.text: If nominal GDP increases by 15% while the general price level increases by 10%, real GDP will most likely
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP is affected by both prices and output. Approximately, real GDP growth is 15% − 10% = 5%.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to cause cost-push inflation
options: Increase in wages and raw material costs
questions.explanation: Cost-push inflation results when production costs rise, causing firms to increase prices.

questions.text: If the purchasing power of money falls continuously because of inflation, the group most likely to suffer is
options: people holding large amounts of cash
questions.explanation: Inflation reduces the real value of money. People holding cash therefore lose purchasing power.

questions.text: A worker earns ₦300,000 monthly. If the consumer price index rises from 100 to 150 while the worker's nominal salary remains unchanged, the worker's real purchasing power has
questions.explanation: Prices have risen by 50% while income remains unchanged, so the worker's real purchasing power falls.

questions.text: When the central bank increases the required reserve ratio of commercial banks, the likely immediate effect is
options: increased ability of banks to create credit
reduced ability of banks to create credit
increased excess reserves available for lending
questions.explanation: A higher reserve requirement means banks must keep more deposits as reserves, leaving less available for lending and credit creation.

questions.text: The central bank sells government securities to commercial banks and the public. This action is intended primarily to
questions.explanation: Selling securities withdraws money from circulation, thereby reducing liquidity and money supply.

questions.text: Which of the following would make the demand for money for speculative purposes increase
questions.explanation: People may hold money rather than bonds when they expect interest rates to rise, because bond prices are expected to fall.

questions.text: Commercial banks are unable to lend out all their deposits because they are required to maintain
questions.explanation: Banks must maintain reserves to meet withdrawals and satisfy regulatory requirements.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major distinction between a commercial bank and a central bank
options: The central bank acts as banker to the government
Commercial banks control the national money supply directly
Commercial banks are responsible for monetary policy
questions.explanation: The central bank serves as banker and financial adviser to the government, while commercial banks mainly provide banking services to individuals and businesses.

questions.text: A government experiencing a recession is most likely to adopt an expansionary fiscal policy by
questions.explanation: Expansionary fiscal policy increases aggregate demand through higher government spending and/or lower taxes.

questions.text: One major disadvantage of financing a persistent budget deficit through excessive borrowing is that it may
questions.explanation: Continuous borrowing increases the government's debt burden and therefore future debt-servicing costs.

questions.text: A tax imposed on the income of a company is classified as
questions.explanation: Company income tax is imposed directly on the income/profits of the company, making it a direct tax.

questions.text: If a tax is imposed on a commodity whose demand is highly inelastic, the greater burden of the tax is likely to fall on
questions.explanation: When demand is highly inelastic, consumers do not reduce purchases much when prices rise, so more of the tax burden can be passed to consumers.

questions.text: The principle of taxation which requires that taxpayers should know how much they are expected to pay and when payment is due is the principle of
questions.explanation: The principle of certainty requires that the amount, time and method of taxation should be clear to taxpayers.

questions.text: If a country's exports are valued at $30 billion and its imports at $36 billion, the country has
options: a balance of trade surplus of $66 billion
questions.explanation: Imports exceed exports by $6 billion, giving the country a trade deficit of $6 billion.

questions.text: A depreciation of a country's currency is most likely to encourage
questions.explanation: Currency depreciation makes domestic goods cheaper to foreigners and imported goods more expensive to domestic consumers.

questions.text: If the Nigerian naira depreciates against the US dollar, the immediate effect on Nigerian importers purchasing goods priced in dollars is likely to be
questions.explanation: A weaker naira means more naira is required to purchase the same amount of dollars, increasing the local cost of imports.

questions.text: A country may impose an import quota primarily to
options: restrict the quantity of goods entering the country
questions.explanation: An import quota is a quantitative restriction placed on the amount of a commodity that can be imported.

questions.text: The theory of comparative advantage provides a justification for international trade because countries can
options: produce everything at lower absolute cost
gain from specialization even when one country is more efficient in producing all goods
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage shows that mutual gains from specialization and trade are possible even when one country has absolute advantage in all goods.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to improve a country's balance of payments position in the long run
questions.explanation: Increasing productive exports generates foreign exchange earnings, which can strengthen the external position.

questions.text: If a country's population grows faster than its real national income, its per capita income will most likely
questions.explanation: Per capita income = National income ÷ Population. If population grows faster than income, income per person falls.

questions.text: A developing country experiences rapid economic growth but widespread poverty remains. This situation suggests that
options: growth automatically guarantees equal income distribution
economic growth and economic development are exactly identical
growth may occur without significant improvement in income distribution
questions.explanation: Economic growth can occur alongside poverty if its benefits are unequally distributed and living conditions do not improve broadly.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to promote human capital development
questions.explanation: Education and healthcare improve the skills, productivity and physical well-being of the population.

questions.text: The dependency ratio of a country is likely to increase when
options: the proportion of children and elderly people increases
questions.explanation: A higher proportion of people outside the working-age population increases the number of dependants relative to workers.

questions.text: A major reason why agricultural productivity may remain low in a developing economy is
options: inadequate extension services and improved inputs
questions.explanation: Limited access to improved seeds, fertilizers, extension services, machinery and finance can keep agricultural productivity low.

questions.text: One major advantage of large-scale mechanized farming over traditional subsistence farming is that it
options: can achieve higher output per worker
questions.explanation: Mechanization can significantly increase labour productivity and the scale of production.

questions.text: A cooperative society differs from a private profit-maximizing firm because its primary objective is to
options: maximize the welfare and economic interests of members
prevent members from participating in decisions
questions.explanation: Cooperatives are established mainly to promote the common economic interests of their members.

questions.text: If a public enterprise is consistently making losses because of political interference and inefficient management, privatization may be considered because it could
options: guarantee that the enterprise will never fail
introduce stronger profit and efficiency incentives
make the enterprise part of the government
questions.explanation: Privatization may introduce private-sector incentives, accountability and efficiency, although it does not guarantee success.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains why a country may experience unemployment despite having available labour
options: Jobs may not be available in the locations or skills required
Wages have no effect on employment
questions.explanation: Structural and geographical mismatches can occur when workers' skills or locations do not correspond with available jobs.

questions.text: Frictional unemployment is most likely to occur when
options: workers are temporarily searching for new jobs
workers permanently lose their jobs because of technology
the entire economy experiences a depression
questions.explanation: Frictional unemployment occurs during the normal process of moving between jobs or entering the labour market.

questions.text: If the government increases expenditure on roads, electricity and water supply, the most likely long-run effect is
questions.explanation: Infrastructure investment can reduce production costs and improve productivity and the economy's productive capacity.

questions.text: An economy is said to be experiencing stagflation when it simultaneously experiences
questions.explanation: Stagflation combines stagnant economic conditions, particularly high unemployment or weak growth, with high inflation.

questions.text: A government wants to reduce inflation without causing a severe fall in employment. Which policy combination would be most appropriate
options: Extremely large increases in government expenditure
Moderate demand management combined with measures that increase productive capacity
Unlimited expansion of the money supply
questions.explanation: Controlling excessive demand can reduce inflation, while increasing productive capacity and supply can help limit the negative effect on employment and output.

questions.text: A consumer has an income of ₦120,000 and spends ₦72,000 on food, ₦24,000 on transport and saves the remaining amount. What percentage of the consumer's income is saved
A consumer's demand for a commodity falls from 500 units to 400 units following an increase in its price from ₦100 to ₦125. Using the original-value method, the price elasticity of demand is
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity = 100/500 × 100 = 20%. Percentage change in price = 25/100 × 100 = 25%. PED = 20/25 = 0.8.

questions.text: A firm reduces the price of its product by 10%, and its total revenue increases by 5%. This suggests that the demand for the product is
questions.explanation: When price falls and total revenue rises, demand is elastic because quantity demanded responds proportionately more than price.

questions.text: Which of the following changes would cause a movement from one point to another along the same production possibility curve
options: Reallocation of existing resources between two goods
questions.explanation: A movement along the PPC results from reallocating existing resources between alternative uses. Changes that increase productive capacity shift the PPC.

questions.text: A farmer can produce either 200 tonnes of maize or 100 tonnes of rice using the same resources. If the farmer produces 150 tonnes of maize, the opportunity cost in terms of rice, assuming a constant opportunity cost, is
questions.explanation: Giving up 200 tonnes of maize allows 100 tonnes of rice. Therefore, producing 150 tonnes of maize sacrifices 50 tonnes of rice.

questions.text: If the price of a complementary commodity increases substantially, the demand for the related commodity will most likely
questions.explanation: Complementary goods are consumed together. A rise in the price of one makes the combination more expensive, thereby reducing demand for the other.

questions.text: A fall in the price of a commodity causes quantity supplied to fall. This is best described as
questions.explanation: A movement along the supply curve caused by a fall in the commodity's own price is called a contraction in supply.

questions.text: If the cost of raw materials used in producing a commodity increases, the supply curve for the commodity will most likely
questions.explanation: Higher input costs reduce profitability at existing prices, causing producers to supply less. The supply curve therefore shifts leftward.

questions.text: A producer increases output from 1,000 units to 1,200 units after employing an additional worker. If the total output before employing the worker was 1,000 units, the worker's marginal product is
questions.explanation: Marginal product is the additional output resulting from an additional factor: 1,200 − 1,000 = 200 units.

questions.text: A firm has fixed costs of ₦50,000. When it produces 2,000 units, its variable cost is ₦150,000. What is its average total cost
A firm operating under perfect competition cannot influence the market price mainly because
options: it faces a perfectly elastic demand curve
entry into the industry is restricted
questions.explanation: An individual perfectly competitive firm is a price taker because it is too small relative to the market and faces a perfectly elastic demand curve at the market price.

questions.text: A monopolist may practise price discrimination when it
options: charges every consumer exactly the same price
sells identical units at different prices to different consumers based on market conditions
questions.explanation: Price discrimination occurs when a seller charges different prices for the same or similar product to different consumers or markets, not solely because of cost differences.

questions.text: A major reason why price discrimination is difficult under perfect competition is that
questions.explanation: Competitive firms have little or no control over price, making systematic price discrimination difficult.

questions.text: When a firm's average cost continues to fall as output expands in the long run, the firm is experiencing
questions.explanation: Economies of scale occur when long-run average cost falls as the scale of production increases.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to result from diseconomies of scale
questions.explanation: Very large firms may experience coordination and communication problems, causing average costs to rise.

questions.text: A worker's wage increases from ₦80,000 to ₦100,000 while the general price level rises by 25%. The worker's real wage has
questions.explanation: Nominal wage increased by 25%, exactly matching the 25% rise in prices. Therefore, the worker's real purchasing power is approximately unchanged.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to redistribute income from high-income earners to low-income earners
questions.explanation: Progressive taxation takes a larger proportion of income from higher earners, while government spending can provide benefits to lower-income groups.

questions.text: A tax system is described as regressive when
options: the tax rate rises as income rises
low-income earners pay a larger proportion of their income than high-income earners
government revenue falls as income increases
questions.explanation: In a regressive system, the tax burden as a percentage of income falls as income rises.

questions.text: If the government increases its expenditure while keeping taxation unchanged, the immediate effect is most likely to be
options: a reduction in money supply automatically
a fall in national income automatically
questions.explanation: Government expenditure is a component of aggregate demand. Increasing it tends to increase aggregate demand.

questions.text: A government pursuing a contractionary fiscal policy is most likely to
questions.explanation: Contractionary fiscal policy reduces aggregate demand through higher taxes and/or lower government spending.

questions.text: If the marginal propensity to consume is 0.75, the simple expenditure multiplier is
If an increase in investment of ₦20 billion produces a total increase in national income of ₦100 billion, the multiplier is
questions.explanation: Multiplier = Change in income ÷ Change in investment = ₦100bn ÷ ₦20bn = 5.

questions.text: If the marginal propensity to save is 0.2, the value of the simple investment multiplier is
questions.explanation: Multiplier = 1/MPS = 1/0.2 = 5.

questions.text: An increase in government expenditure financed entirely by borrowing is most likely to cause
questions.explanation: Borrowing allows government to increase spending without an immediate equivalent increase in taxation, thereby raising aggregate demand.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT included when calculating GDP using the expenditure approach
questions.explanation: Transfer payments, such as certain pensions or welfare payments, do not represent payment for current production, so they are excluded from GDP expenditure calculations.

questions.text: If GDP is ₦80 trillion and depreciation is ₦10 trillion, the value of net domestic product is
questions.explanation: NDP = GDP − depreciation = ₦80tn − ₦10tn = ₦70tn.

questions.text: Which of the following would cause nominal GDP to rise without necessarily causing an increase in real output
options: Increase in the general price level
Increase in employment with unchanged prices
questions.explanation: Nominal GDP is measured at current prices, so it can rise simply because prices increase even when physical output does not.

questions.text: The existence of a large informal sector makes national income estimation difficult because
options: all informal activities are recorded twice
many transactions are not formally recorded
informal workers always earn more than formal workers
questions.explanation: Many informal economic activities are unrecorded or poorly documented, making accurate estimation difficult.

questions.text: Which combination is most likely to increase the standard of living in a developing country
options: Higher real income per capita and improved social services
Higher population growth and stagnant output
questions.explanation: Standard of living depends on factors such as real income per capita, healthcare, education, housing and access to essential services.

questions.text: A country has a high GDP per capita but a very unequal distribution of income. This suggests that
options: all citizens necessarily have a high standard of living
GDP per capita alone may give a misleading picture of welfare
the country cannot have economic growth
questions.explanation: GDP per capita is an average and does not reveal how income is distributed.

questions.text: Which of the following policies is most appropriate for reducing structural unemployment
questions.explanation: Structural unemployment results from a mismatch between workers' skills and available jobs. Retraining can reduce this mismatch.

questions.text: If the working population of a country is 20 million and 2 million are unemployed, the unemployment rate is
questions.explanation: Unemployment rate = 2m ÷ 20m × 100 = 10%.

questions.text: A worker who voluntarily leaves one job and spends several weeks searching for another is experiencing
questions.explanation: Frictional unemployment occurs during job search and transitions between jobs.

questions.text: Disguised unemployment is particularly associated with situations where
options: some workers have zero or very low marginal productivity
unemployment is officially recorded at zero
questions.explanation: Disguised unemployment occurs when more workers are employed than necessary, so removing some workers would have little or no effect on total output.

questions.text: If a country's exports are ₦15 billion, imports are ₦20 billion, and it receives ₦8 billion in net invisible earnings, its trade balance is
questions.explanation: Trade balance considers visible exports and imports: ₦15bn − ₦20bn = ₦5bn deficit. Invisible earnings affect the broader balance of payments, not the visible trade balance.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a visible export
questions.explanation: Visible trade involves physical goods. Crude oil is a tangible exported commodity.

questions.text: A country whose currency is overvalued is likely to experience
questions.explanation: An overvalued currency makes domestic goods more expensive to foreigners while imports become relatively cheaper.

questions.text: A fall in the exchange rate of the naira from ₦1,000/$ to ₦1,200/$ means that
options: the dollar has become cheaper in naira terms
the naira has depreciated against the dollar
the purchasing power of the dollar has fallen in Nigeria
questions.explanation: More naira is now required to purchase one dollar, indicating naira depreciation.

questions.text: A central bank may raise the bank rate during a period of excessive inflation in order to
options: encourage commercial banks to borrow more cheaply
discourage borrowing and reduce credit expansion
questions.explanation: A higher bank rate makes borrowing more expensive, helping to reduce credit creation and aggregate demand.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to increase the money multiplier
options: Increase in cash held by banks
questions.explanation: A lower reserve requirement allows banks to lend a larger proportion of deposits, increasing the money multiplier.

questions.text: The lender of last resort function of a central bank means that it
options: provides emergency funds to financial institutions facing liquidity problems
gives free loans to all businesses
questions.explanation: The central bank can provide emergency liquidity to commercial banks when they face temporary difficulties meeting their obligations.

questions.text: Which of the following is a major reason for holding foreign exchange reserves
options: To meet international payment obligations and support exchange-rate stability
questions.explanation: Foreign reserves help a country meet external payment obligations and can be used to manage foreign exchange pressures.

questions.text: A country imposes a high tariff on imported finished goods while allowing raw materials to enter at low tariffs. The policy is primarily designed to
questions.explanation: Cheap imported inputs combined with protection on finished goods can help domestic manufacturers compete with imported finished products.

questions.text: One possible disadvantage of protectionism is that it may
options: increase prices and reduce consumer choice
questions.explanation: Protection can reduce foreign competition, potentially allowing domestic firms to charge higher prices and offer fewer choices.

questions.text: The infant-industry argument for protectionism is based on the belief that
options: all domestic industries are permanently inefficient
newly established industries need temporary protection to become competitive
exports are harmful to economic growth
questions.explanation: Infant industries may need temporary protection until they achieve economies of scale and become competitive.

questions.text: A major limitation of agriculture in many developing economies is the seasonal nature of production. This can result in
options: fluctuations in agricultural prices and farmers' incomes
questions.explanation: Seasonal production can create periods of surplus and scarcity, causing fluctuations in prices and farmers' incomes.

questions.text: Which of the following policies would most directly encourage farmers to increase agricultural investment
options: Removal of all rural credit facilities
questions.explanation: Affordable credit enables farmers to invest in machinery, improved seeds, fertilizers and other productive inputs.

questions.text: A country discovers a large deposit of crude oil. In the short run, this is most likely to
options: increase potential government revenue and foreign exchange earnings
questions.explanation: Petroleum exports can generate substantial foreign exchange and government revenue, although dependence on one resource creates other risks.

questions.text: A country becomes heavily dependent on one primary export commodity. A major danger of this situation is that
options: fluctuations in world prices can cause large changes in national income
questions.explanation: Dependence on one commodity exposes the economy to international price fluctuations, which can cause instability in export earnings and government revenue.

questions.text: A developing country wants sustainable long-term economic development. Which combination of policies would best support this objective
options: Heavy dependence on one export commodity and low investment in education
Investment in human capital, infrastructure, productive industries and economic diversification
Continuous borrowing for consumption without productive investment
questions.explanation: Sustainable development requires improving human capital, infrastructure, productive capacity and economic diversification, rather than relying on a single source of income.

questions.text: A consumer has ₦60,000 to spend on commodities X and Y. The price of X is ₦3,000 while that of Y is ₦2,000. If the consumer spends the entire income on X, the maximum quantity of X that can be purchased is
questions.explanation: Maximum quantity = ₦60,000 ÷ ₦3,000 = 20 units.

questions.text: A consumer's income increases from ₦100,000 to ₦120,000, while the quantity demanded of a commodity rises from 40 units to 44 units. The income elasticity of demand is
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity = 4/40 × 100 = 10%. Income change = 20%. Income elasticity = 10/20 = 0.5. The commodity is therefore a normal necessity.

questions.text: If the price of a commodity falls from ₦500 to ₦400 and total expenditure by consumers rises from ₦100,000 to ₦120,000, the demand for the commodity is
questions.explanation: A fall in price accompanied by an increase in total expenditure indicates elastic demand.

questions.text: Which of the following would cause both the equilibrium price and quantity of a normal commodity to increase, assuming other factors remain constant
questions.explanation: An increase in demand shifts the demand curve rightward, causing both equilibrium price and quantity to rise, assuming supply is unchanged.

questions.text: If improved technology reduces the cost of producing a commodity while demand remains unchanged, the new equilibrium will most likely involve
questions.explanation: Improved technology increases supply, shifting the supply curve rightward. Equilibrium price falls while quantity rises.

questions.text: A government decides to guarantee farmers a minimum price above the equilibrium price of an agricultural product. The most likely consequence is
questions.explanation: A price floor above equilibrium encourages producers to supply more while consumers demand less, creating excess supply or surplus.

questions.text: The government may purchase the surplus created by an agricultural price support programme mainly to
options: prevent the guaranteed price from collapsing
questions.explanation: Government purchases can absorb excess supply and help maintain the guaranteed minimum price.

questions.text: A major reason why agricultural products often have unstable prices is that their supply is
options: highly responsive to changes in technology only
affected by weather and other natural conditions
questions.explanation: Agricultural output depends heavily on rainfall, pests, diseases and other unpredictable natural conditions, causing supply fluctuations.

questions.text: If the price of a commodity is ₦50 and 10,000 units are sold, while total variable cost is ₦300,000 and fixed cost is ₦100,000, the firm's profit is
A firm will continue producing in the short run even when making a loss if its revenue is sufficient to cover its
questions.explanation: In the short run, a firm may continue operating if it can cover its variable costs, because fixed costs must be paid regardless of output.

questions.text: A firm has total revenue of ₦800,000 and total cost of ₦650,000. Its economic profit is
questions.explanation: Economic profit = Total revenue − Total economic cost = ₦150,000.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to be an external economy of scale
options: Bulk purchasing by a single firm
Development of specialized suppliers in an industrial area
Reduction in a firm's internal administrative costs
questions.explanation: External economies arise from the growth of the industry or location, benefiting firms collectively. Specialized suppliers are an example.

questions.text: A monopolist differs from a perfectly competitive firm because the monopolist
questions.explanation: A monopolist is a price maker, although its ability to raise price is constrained by demand and substitutes.

questions.text: A monopoly may persist in an industry when a firm controls an essential raw material. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Control over a key resource can prevent potential competitors from entering, creating an ownership barrier to entry.

questions.text: In an oligopolistic market, one firm's decision to reduce its price may cause competitors to reduce theirs because firms are
questions.explanation: Oligopolistic firms are interdependent because each firm's actions can significantly affect its competitors.

questions.text: Product differentiation is most closely associated with
questions.explanation: Firms under monopolistic competition sell products that are similar but differentiated by brand, quality, packaging or other characteristics.

questions.text: Which of the following is a necessary condition for a firm to practise price discrimination successfully
options: Consumers must be unable to resell the product easily
The firm must have no market power
Demand must be perfectly elastic everywhere
questions.explanation: If consumers can easily resell a cheaper product to others, the seller cannot maintain different prices. Market separation is therefore important.

questions.text: If the marginal cost of producing an additional unit is greater than marginal revenue, a profit-maximizing firm should
questions.explanation: When MC > MR, producing another unit adds more to cost than revenue. The firm should reduce output until MC and MR are balanced.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to cause an increase in labour productivity
options: Improved technology and better worker skills
questions.explanation: Better technology, training and capital equipment enable workers to produce more output per unit of labour.

questions.text: The mobility of labour from one occupation to another is known as
questions.explanation: Occupational mobility refers to the ability of labour to move between different types of jobs or occupations.

questions.text: A major factor limiting geographical mobility of labour is
options: family ties and high relocation costs
questions.explanation: Workers may be unable or unwilling to relocate because of family commitments, housing costs and relocation expenses.

questions.text: The reward for capital as a factor of production is
questions.explanation: The conventional reward for the use of capital is interest.

questions.text: Economic rent is best described as
options: payment made only for the use of buildings
payment to a factor of production in excess of its transfer earnings
questions.explanation: Economic rent is the amount earned by a factor above what is necessary to keep it in its current use.

questions.text: If a worker can earn ₦200,000 in his present occupation but would accept ₦150,000 to work elsewhere, his transfer earnings are
questions.explanation: Transfer earnings are the minimum payment required to keep a factor in its current use. Here, the worker's current alternative earning is ₦200,000.

questions.text: Which of the following would most likely increase the supply of skilled labour in an economy
options: Increased investment in technical and vocational education
questions.explanation: Education and vocational training increase workers' skills and employability, expanding the supply of skilled labour.

questions.text: If a country's nominal national income increases by 20% while the general price level increases by 20%, real national income will approximately
questions.explanation: If nominal income and prices increase at approximately the same rate, real income remains broadly unchanged.

questions.text: Which of the following is a limitation of using per capita income as a measure of economic welfare
options: It does not reveal income distribution
It can be calculated from national income
questions.explanation: Per capita income is an average and may hide large inequalities in income distribution.

questions.text: If the population of a country increases from 50 million to 55 million while real national income remains constant, real income per capita will
questions.explanation: With the same national income spread among more people, income per person falls.

questions.text: Which of the following transactions would be included in current GDP
options: Sale of a used car produced five years ago
Purchase of shares on the stock exchange
Transfer of money from parents to children
questions.explanation: Construction of a new factory represents current production and investment, so it is included in GDP.

questions.text: The double-counting problem in national income accounting occurs when
options: intermediate goods are counted more than once
questions.explanation: Counting the value of intermediate goods separately alongside final goods would overstate national output.

questions.text: The value-added method avoids double counting by measuring
options: the increase in value contributed at each stage of production
questions.explanation: Value added measures the additional value created at each stage, preventing intermediate products from being counted repeatedly.

questions.text: If the consumer price index rises from 120 to 150, the rate of inflation over the period is
A government seeking to reduce demand-pull inflation could
options: increase taxation and reduce government spending
questions.explanation: Higher taxation and lower government expenditure reduce aggregate demand, helping to control demand-pull inflation.

questions.text: Cost-push inflation can be reduced in the long run by
options: improving productivity and reducing production bottlenecks
increasing import restrictions regardless of circumstances
questions.explanation: Improving productivity and supply conditions can reduce unit production costs and supply-side inflationary pressure.

questions.text: Which group is most likely to benefit from unexpected inflation
options: People living entirely on fixed pensions
People holding large amounts of cash
questions.explanation: Inflation reduces the real value of money, so borrowers repay fixed debts with money that has lower purchasing power.

questions.text: The primary function of a central bank in relation to the banking system is to
options: provide ordinary current accounts to every citizen
questions.explanation: Central banks regulate the banking system, supervise banks and conduct monetary policy.

questions.text: If the central bank reduces the discount rate, commercial banks are likely to
options: find borrowing from the central bank more expensive
increase their willingness to borrow and lend
questions.explanation: A lower discount/bank rate makes central-bank borrowing cheaper, potentially encouraging credit expansion.

questions.text: Which of the following would most likely reduce the ability of commercial banks to create credit
options: Increase in excess reserves available for lending
Increase in deposits without any regulatory change
questions.explanation: A higher reserve requirement means banks must retain more deposits and therefore have less available for lending.

questions.text: Money performs the function of a unit of account because it
options: can be used to store wealth
provides a common measure for expressing the value of goods and services
questions.explanation: As a unit of account, money provides a standard measure of value, allowing prices to be compared.

questions.text: If people lose confidence in a country's currency and begin to use foreign currencies for transactions, the domestic currency is losing its function as
questions.explanation: A currency serves as a medium of exchange when people accept it for transactions. Loss of confidence undermines this function.

questions.text: A country's balance of payments can be improved by
options: increasing productive exports and reducing excessive imports
questions.explanation: Increasing exports brings in foreign exchange, while reducing unnecessary imports reduces foreign exchange outflows.

questions.text: Which of the following is recorded in the current account of the balance of payments
options: Export and import of goods and services
Purchase of domestic shares by residents only
Changes in central bank reserves only
questions.explanation: The current account includes trade in goods and services, as well as income and certain transfers.

questions.text: A country has a persistent current-account deficit. One possible consequence is
options: continuous accumulation of foreign reserves without borrowing
automatic appreciation of the domestic currency
questions.explanation: A persistent external deficit means the country may need capital inflows, borrowing or reserve drawdowns to finance it.

questions.text: A country that specializes in producing a commodity for which it has a comparative advantage is likely to
options: increase efficiency and gain from international exchange
questions.explanation: Specialization according to comparative advantage allows countries to use resources more efficiently and gain through trade.

questions.text: Which of the following is an argument against unrestricted international trade
options: It may expose infant industries to intense foreign competition
It permits countries to obtain goods they cannot efficiently produce
questions.explanation: Newly established domestic industries may struggle against established foreign producers with lower costs and greater economies of scale.

questions.text: A quota differs from a tariff because a quota
options: directly limits the physical quantity of imports
questions.explanation: A quota is a quantitative restriction, while a tariff is a tax imposed on imported goods.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to encourage rural-urban migration
options: Greater perceived employment opportunities in urban areas
questions.explanation: People often migrate when they believe cities offer better jobs, income and social opportunities.

questions.text: Rapid rural-urban migration without adequate urban planning may result in
questions.explanation: Rapid migration can place pressure on housing, transport and employment, contributing to overcrowding and urban unemployment.

questions.text: A country that relies heavily on agriculture for employment but has low agricultural productivity may experience
questions.explanation: Low productivity can mean that many workers are engaged in agriculture but contribute relatively little additional output, resulting in underemployment and disguised unemployment.

questions.text: A government wants to reduce excessive dependence on crude oil while maintaining economic growth. Which policy is most appropriate
options: Diversify into manufacturing, agriculture and other productive sectors
questions.explanation: Economic diversification reduces vulnerability to fluctuations in crude-oil prices while creating alternative sources of employment, output and foreign exchange.

questions.text: A consumer's monthly income increases from ₦200,000 to ₦240,000. During the same period, the quantity of a commodity purchased rises from 50 units to 55 units. Based on the original-value method, the income elasticity of demand is
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity = 5/50 × 100 = 10%. Percentage change in income = 40,000/200,000 × 100 = 20%. Income elasticity = 10/20 = 0.5.

questions.text: A commodity has a price elasticity of demand of 2.5. If its price is reduced by 8%, the quantity demanded will approximately
questions.explanation: PED = % change in quantity ÷ % change in price. Therefore, quantity change = 2.5 × 8% = 20% increase because price falls.

questions.text: The demand for a product is relatively inelastic. If the producer wants to increase total revenue, the most appropriate action is to
options: increase the price of substitutes only
questions.explanation: With inelastic demand, a price increase causes a proportionately smaller reduction in quantity demanded, so total revenue increases.

questions.text: If the price of commodity X rises from ₦100 to ₦120 and its quantity supplied increases from 500 to 600 units, the price elasticity of supply using the original-value method is
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity supplied = 100/500 = 20%. Percentage change in price = 20/100 = 20%. PES = 1.0, meaning unitary elasticity.

questions.text: The supply of agricultural products is often relatively inelastic in the short run because farmers
options: can immediately change the size of their farms
cannot easily adjust production to price changes within a short period
questions.explanation: Agricultural production often requires time for crops and livestock to mature, making short-run supply relatively unresponsive to price changes.

questions.text: If both demand and supply for a commodity increase simultaneously, which of the following can be determined with certainty
questions.explanation: Both an increase in demand and an increase in supply tend to increase equilibrium quantity. The effect on price is uncertain, depending on the relative shifts.

questions.text: A shortage of a commodity occurs when, at the prevailing price
questions.explanation: A shortage occurs when consumers want to buy more than producers are willing to supply at the existing price.

questions.text: A market price of ₦1,500 results in demand of 8,000 units and supply of 8,000 units. If demand subsequently rises to 10,000 units while supply remains unchanged at the original price, the market will experience
questions.explanation: At ₦1,500, quantity demanded becomes 10,000 while supply remains 8,000, creating a 2,000-unit shortage.

questions.text: A firm has a total cost of ₦500,000 at an output of 10,000 units. When output rises to 12,000 units, total cost becomes ₦560,000. The marginal cost of the additional output is
A firm produces 500 units at an average variable cost of ₦40 and has total fixed cost of ₦10,000. Its total cost is
If a firm's average fixed cost falls as output increases, this occurs because
options: the same fixed cost is spread over more units
questions.explanation: Fixed cost remains constant in the short run, so producing more units spreads that cost over a larger quantity of output.

questions.text: A firm is operating at the profit-maximizing level of output when
questions.explanation: The standard profit-maximization condition is MR = MC, provided the firm is producing at an economically viable output level.

questions.text: A monopolist faces a downward-sloping demand curve because
options: it sells to a market with no consumers
it is the sole seller and must reduce price to sell more output
questions.explanation: Since a monopolist faces the market demand curve, selling additional units generally requires lowering the price.

questions.text: Which of the following would most likely make a monopoly less powerful
questions.explanation: Close substitutes limit a monopolist's ability to raise prices because consumers can switch to alternatives.

questions.text: A major advantage of competition in a market economy is that it tends to
options: encourage firms to improve efficiency and quality
questions.explanation: Competition pressures firms to reduce costs, improve quality and innovate in order to retain customers.

questions.text: If a firm's total revenue is ₦2 million and its explicit costs are ₦1.2 million while its implicit costs are ₦500,000, its economic profit is
questions.explanation: Total economic cost = ₦1.2m + ₦0.5m = ₦1.7m. Economic profit = ₦2m − ₦1.7m = ₦300,000.

questions.text: A country's real GDP rises from ₦40 trillion to ₦44 trillion while its population rises from 100 million to 110 million. Real GDP per capita has
questions.explanation: Initially, per capita GDP = ₦40tn/100m = ₦400,000. New figure = ₦44tn/110m = ₦400,000. Therefore, it is unchanged.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to cause an increase in real GDP
options: A rise in prices with unchanged output
An increase in actual production of final goods and services
A rise in the general price level only
An increase in imported second-hand goods
questions.explanation: Real GDP measures changes in actual output after removing the effect of price changes.

questions.text: If nominal GDP increases by 30% while the GDP deflator increases by 20%, real output has
questions.explanation: Nominal output rose faster than prices, implying that real output increased.

questions.text: Which of the following is excluded from the calculation of national income because it does not represent payment for current productive activity
questions.explanation: Transfer payments are not payments for current production, so they are excluded from national income.

questions.text: If an economy's national income increases while its population increases at a faster rate, the country is likely to experience
options: an increase in per capita income
a fall in per capita income
questions.explanation: Since population grows faster than national income, income available per person decreases.

questions.text: Which of the following would make national income figures more reliable in a developing economy
options: Improved statistical records and coverage of informal activities
questions.explanation: Better statistical systems and inclusion of previously unrecorded activities produce more accurate national income estimates.

questions.text: If the general price level increases from 100 to 125 while nominal income remains unchanged, the purchasing power of money will
questions.explanation: Higher prices mean the same amount of money can buy fewer goods and services, so purchasing power falls.

questions.text: A country experiencing hyperinflation is likely to face
options: rapid erosion of the currency's purchasing power
increased real value of cash balances
questions.explanation: Hyperinflation is an extremely rapid rise in prices, causing the currency's purchasing power to collapse.

questions.text: If the government increases money supply substantially while output remains unchanged, the most likely long-run consequence is
questions.explanation: If money supply increases faster than real output, excessive demand can place upward pressure on prices.

questions.text: A government may use an open market sale of securities during inflation because the policy
questions.explanation: When the central bank sells securities, buyers pay money to the central bank, reducing liquidity and money available for spending.

questions.text: If the cash reserve ratio is reduced, commercial banks can potentially
options: lend a larger proportion of deposits
lend a smaller proportion of deposits
questions.explanation: A lower reserve requirement releases more funds for lending, potentially increasing credit creation.

questions.text: The central bank is described as the lender of last resort because it
options: provides emergency loans when banks cannot obtain funds elsewhere
questions.explanation: During liquidity crises, the central bank can provide emergency funding to financial institutions.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to increase the demand for money for transactions
options: Fall in the volume of economic activity
questions.explanation: Higher income generally means more transactions, increasing the transaction demand for money.

questions.text: A country adopts a progressive income tax system primarily to
options: make the tax burden proportional to consumption only
make higher-income earners contribute a larger proportion of their income
ensure everyone pays the same amount
questions.explanation: Progressive taxation imposes a higher tax rate on higher levels of income and can promote income redistribution.

questions.text: An indirect tax differs from a direct tax because an indirect tax
options: cannot be shifted to another person
is imposed on expenditure or goods and may be passed on to consumers
is imposed only on personal income
questions.explanation: Indirect taxes, such as VAT, are imposed on goods and services and can often be shifted through prices to consumers.

questions.text: The burden of an indirect tax is likely to fall more heavily on consumers when
questions.explanation: With inelastic demand, consumers reduce purchases only slightly when prices rise, allowing producers to pass a greater portion of the tax onto consumers.

questions.text: A government budget surplus occurs when
questions.explanation: A budget surplus exists when government revenue is greater than government expenditure.

questions.text: If government expenditure is ₦8 trillion and government revenue is ₦6.5 trillion, the budget position is
questions.explanation: Deficit = ₦8tn − ₦6.5tn = ₦1.5tn.

questions.text: A government may deliberately operate a budget deficit during a recession in order to
questions.explanation: Deficit spending can increase aggregate demand, encouraging production and employment during a recession.

questions.text: If a country exports goods worth $50 billion and imports goods worth $40 billion, while it pays $15 billion for foreign services, its visible trade balance is
questions.explanation: Visible trade balance considers goods only: $50bn − $40bn = $10bn surplus. Services belong to invisible trade.

questions.text: A depreciation of a country's currency is more likely to improve its trade balance when
options: exports and imports are completely unresponsive to price changes
demand for exports and imports responds sufficiently to price changes
the country imports everything and exports nothing
questions.explanation: Depreciation improves competitiveness, but the trade balance improves more effectively when quantities of exports and imports respond to the changed relative prices.

questions.text: A country may deliberately restrict imports to protect its domestic industries, but a possible long-run disadvantage is
options: reduced efficiency and higher domestic prices
questions.explanation: Reduced competition can allow inefficient domestic firms to survive, resulting in higher costs and prices.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the concept of comparative advantage
options: A country produces every commodity at a lower money cost
A country produces a commodity at a lower opportunity cost than another country
A country exports only goods it cannot produce
A country has the largest population
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage is determined by relative opportunity cost, not necessarily absolute production cost.

questions.text: Country A can produce either 100 units of wheat or 200 units of rice using the same resources. Country B can produce either 120 units of wheat or 120 units of rice. Which country has the comparative advantage in wheat
questions.explanation: For A, the opportunity cost of 1 wheat = 2 rice. For B, 1 wheat = 1 rice. Since B sacrifices fewer rice units to produce wheat, Country B has the comparative advantage in wheat.

questions.text: A student has ₦30,000 and can either purchase Economics textbooks or use the money to attend a computer training programme. If the student chooses the textbooks, the opportunity cost of the decision is
options: the knowledge obtained from the textbooks
the total utility derived from the textbooks
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the next best alternative forgone when a choice is made.

questions.text: A country's production possibility curve shifts outward after the discovery of new mineral resources. This indicates that
questions.explanation: An outward shift of the PPC indicates an increase in the economy's productive capacity, usually resulting from more resources, better technology or improved productivity.

questions.text: If a country's resources are fully employed and it decides to produce more capital goods at the expense of consumer goods, this illustrates
questions.explanation: Producing more capital goods requires sacrificing some consumer goods. The sacrificed output represents the opportunity cost.

questions.text: A consumer purchases more of commodity X when the price of commodity Y rises. The most likely relationship between X and Y is that they are
questions.explanation: If the price of Y rises, consumers switch toward X. This indicates that X and Y are substitutes.

questions.text: A fall in the price of a commodity causes an increase in the quantity demanded, while all other factors remain unchanged. This is described as
questions.explanation: A fall in the commodity's own price causes movement down the same demand curve, known as an extension of demand.

questions.text: If consumers suddenly develop a strong preference for a commodity, while its price remains unchanged, the immediate effect will be
options: a rightward shift of the demand curve
a leftward shift of the supply curve
questions.explanation: A change in taste or preference is a non-price determinant of demand, causing the demand curve to shift.

questions.text: A producer expects the price of a commodity to rise significantly next month. If the commodity can be stored cheaply, the producer may reduce current supply because
options: future prices are expected to be higher
consumers have stopped buying the product
questions.explanation: Producers may withhold stock when they expect higher future prices, especially when storage is possible.

questions.text: If a government imposes a maximum legal price below equilibrium, black-market activities are likely to emerge because
options: there is excess supply at the controlled price
consumers are unwilling to buy the commodity
some consumers are willing to pay more than the legal price
questions.explanation: A price ceiling below equilibrium creates shortage. Some consumers may therefore be willing to pay above the legal price, encouraging black-market transactions.

questions.text: The cross elasticity of demand between two commodities is negative. This implies that the commodities are
questions.explanation: A negative cross elasticity means that an increase in the price of one reduces demand for the other, indicating complementarity.

questions.text: If the income elasticity of demand for a commodity is negative, the commodity is most likely
questions.explanation: Negative income elasticity means demand falls as income rises, which is characteristic of an inferior good.

questions.text: A firm produces 2,000 units at a total cost of ₦900,000. If its total fixed cost is ₦300,000, its average variable cost is
A firm's total cost is ₦1,000,000 when it produces 5,000 units and ₦1,150,000 when output rises to 6,000 units. The marginal cost of the additional 1,000 units is
questions.explanation: Change in total cost = ₦150,000. Change in output = 1,000. Therefore, MC = ₦150 per unit.

questions.text: When average product is increasing, marginal product is generally
questions.explanation: Average product rises whenever marginal product is greater than average product.

questions.text: The point at which marginal product equals average product corresponds to the point where
options: average product is at its maximum
total cost is at its maximum
questions.explanation: Average product reaches its maximum when MP = AP.

questions.text: A firm experiences increasing returns to scale when
options: all inputs increase by 10% and output increases by less than 10%
all inputs increase by 10% and output increases by exactly 10%
all inputs increase by 10% and output increases by more than 10%
output remains unchanged when all inputs increase
questions.explanation: Increasing returns to scale occur when output increases more than proportionately to the increase in all inputs.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an internal economy of scale
options: Development of better transport infrastructure in an industrial region
Availability of specialized banks in an industry
Bulk purchasing of raw materials by a large firm
Expansion of an industry's skilled labour pool
questions.explanation: Bulk purchasing benefits an individual firm because of its larger scale. It is therefore an internal economy of scale.

questions.text: Under perfect competition, a firm's average revenue is equal to
questions.explanation: Average revenue = Total revenue ÷ Quantity. Since TR = Price × Quantity, AR = Price.

questions.text: A perfectly competitive firm earns abnormal profit in the short run when
options: average revenue exceeds average total cost
questions.explanation: Abnormal or economic profit occurs when price/average revenue is greater than average total cost at the profit-maximizing output.

questions.text: A monopolist's marginal revenue curve lies below its demand curve because
options: it must lower price to sell additional units
questions.explanation: To sell more output, a monopolist generally has to reduce price. This causes marginal revenue to be below price/average revenue.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to create a natural monopoly
options: Strong economies of scale over the relevant market range
questions.explanation: A natural monopoly can arise when one large firm can supply the market at lower average cost because of strong economies of scale.

questions.text: A worker is paid ₦50,000 per week. If the general price level rises by 10% while the worker's wage remains unchanged, the worker's real wage will
questions.explanation: Prices have risen while nominal wages remain constant, so the worker's purchasing power decreases.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to increase the supply of labour in an economy
options: Reduction in migration into the labour market
questions.explanation: A larger working-age population increases the potential labour force, assuming people are willing and able to work.

questions.text: If the demand for labour increases while the supply of labour remains unchanged, the equilibrium wage rate will generally
questions.explanation: An increase in labour demand shifts the demand curve rightward, causing the equilibrium wage to rise.

questions.text: A minimum wage fixed above the equilibrium wage may result in
questions.explanation: A wage floor above equilibrium can cause more people to seek work while firms demand less labour, resulting in surplus labour or unemployment.

questions.text: Which of the following would most likely increase the bargaining power of workers
questions.explanation: Trade unions can increase workers' bargaining power by collectively negotiating wages and employment conditions.

questions.text: A trade union may deliberately restrict the supply of labour to an occupation in order to
options: increase the bargaining position of existing members
questions.explanation: Restricting labour supply can increase the scarcity of workers in an occupation and potentially raise wages for existing members.

questions.text: If a country's nominal GDP is ₦120 trillion and the GDP deflator is 150, its real GDP at base-year prices is
questions.explanation: Real GDP = Nominal GDP ÷ (Deflator/100). = ₦120tn ÷ 1.5 = ₦80tn.

questions.text: If real GDP increases while the population remains unchanged, there will most likely be
options: an increase in real GDP per capita
a decrease in real GDP per capita
no change in output per person
questions.explanation: With population constant, higher real GDP means more real output per person.

questions.text: Which of the following would cause nominal GDP to increase without increasing real GDP
options: Increased physical output at constant prices
Increased prices with unchanged physical output
questions.explanation: Higher prices increase nominal GDP even when the economy's physical output remains unchanged.

questions.text: A country records a high GDP growth rate, but unemployment remains high. One possible explanation is that
options: growth is concentrated in capital-intensive sectors
labour productivity has fallen to zero
questions.explanation: Capital-intensive industries may increase output substantially without generating enough employment, resulting in jobless or low-employment growth.

questions.text: If a country's GNP is greater than its GDP, this indicates that
options: foreigners earn more income domestically than citizens earn abroad
citizens earn more factor income abroad than foreigners earn domestically
questions.explanation: GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad. Therefore, GNP exceeds GDP when domestic residents' factor income from abroad exceeds foreigners' factor income earned domestically.

questions.text: Which of the following is likely to reduce the quality of national income estimates
questions.explanation: Subsistence and informal activities may not be fully recorded, causing underestimation or inaccuracies in national income.

questions.text: If the marginal propensity to consume is 0.8, an increase in autonomous investment of ₦10 billion will increase equilibrium income by
questions.explanation: Multiplier = 1/(1 − 0.8) = 5. Income increase = 5 × ₦10bn = ₦50bn.

questions.text: If households decide to save a larger proportion of their income while investment remains unchanged, aggregate demand will initially
questions.explanation: Increased saving means reduced consumption expenditure, which can reduce aggregate demand in the short run.
